text:
maria: Heads up — compliance asked how we'll avoid sending PII to third-party telemetry vendors. Our OTEL spans currently have attributes like user.email, user_id, ip, session_id. Any proposals for exporter-level handling? We need re-identification for incident triage but vendors shouldn't see raw PII. Thoughts?

kevin: I think we have three practical options: 1) redact (drop attrs) 2) irreversible hash (HMAC) 3) encrypt attributes with a per-tenant key so vendor sees ciphertext. Hashing + salt is simplest but not reversible.

raj: For incident triage we sometimes need reversible mapping. Idea: exporter sends hashed value, and we keep a re-id map in a KMS-backed vault that only ops or a security process can access to reidentify when there's an approved request.

sophia: Security note: any re-id map is itself PII and must be treated with the same controls (encryption at rest, strict IAM, audit logs). My preference: default to non-reversible approaches and require explicit enterprise opt-in for any re-identification capability.

alison: From product/console POV — we should expose a per-customer policy: redact | hash | encrypt. Console should show the effective policy, last policy change, and an audit trail entry for who changed it. Also UI to request/approve re-id for an incident.

kevin: Implementation idea: an OTEL collector processor/exporter plugin (call it "redact_hash_exporter") that runs before vendor exporters and can apply actions per-attribute. Sample config below: 

```
processors:
  redact_mask:
    actions:
      - key: user.email
        action: hash
        algorithm: hmac-sha256
        key_ref: \"${CUSTOMER_SALT}\"
      - key: user.ip
        action: mask
      - key: session_id
        action: drop

exporters:
  vendor_x:
    endpoint: https://x.example/ingest

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [redact_mask]
      exporters: [vendor_x]
```

maria: Couple of follow-ups: 1) how do we rotate keys and reflect that in hashes? 2) what retention window do we keep for audit logs and any re-id mappings? Compliance mentioned 90 days audit retention but data retention for PII is typically 30 days.

sophia: Rotation — use KMS key versioning and include key-id or version metadata in the hashed output so we can re-hash/verify if needed. For mappings: if we support them, store encrypted in a vault with TTL/retention policies (auto-delete). Prefer default: do NOT store mappings unless customer explicitly opts in and signs off on the compliance risk.

raj: Additional thought: do allowlist hashing for low-risk attributes (e.g., user_id -> hash), but for email or IP offer mask or drop. Also use sampling for any reversible re-id mapping to limit exposure and cost — only store mappings for sampled traces.

alison: UX for rollout — feature flag + staged canary. Start internal-only, then invite a few enterprise customers to opt-in, then GA. Console should let customer admins view and request opt-in, and we need an acceptance workflow (legal/compliance).

ops-bot: ticket created: INF-9272 "telemetry: redact/hash/exporter + per-tenant policy + audit logs" by @maria

kevin: Implementation owners? I'll take the collector plugin + unit tests. Maria/Alison can own console UI + rollout UX. Sophia/Raj for security review and KMS integration. I'll open a draft PR and tag @eng-sre for rollout/runbook.

maria: Thanks all — let's sync in infra sync on Thursday to align scope and landing zones. :thumbsup:
